clue.text: A horse might come a cropper here, with finish in sight

definitions.text: A horse might come a cropper here, with finish in sight

parts.words: A horse might come a cropper here, with finish in sight
parts.note: the closing stretch of a racecourse, approaching the winning post, where a tired runner may still fall before the line

explanation.surface: A racing pundit warns that a horse can still tumble even as the winning post comes into view.
explanation.definitionFit: The final run-in of a racecourse before the winning post is its last level stretch, where the finish is in view.

clue.text: Shelter to set up for poor person

parts.note: a haven is a place of shelter or refuge

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the short word to is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a refuge for the destitute.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means read upwards, so the short word is turned round beneath the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A have-not is someone lacking wealth, the opposite of the haves.

clue.text: Gong bringing Duke into dinner, perhaps

indicators.note: into says the letter for Duke is placed inside the word for the dinner

parts.note: dinner is one example of a meal, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A duke is awarded his decoration while dining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gong' is British slang for a medal or decoration, not a dinner gong, despite the dinner nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British informal slang for an award or decoration worn on the chest.

clue.text: Girl's upset about soldiers? That's a reasonable inference

indicators.note: about says the reversed name goes round the word for soldiers
in a down clue, upset means the girl's name with its possessive is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: Molly is a girl's name; with the possessive it gives MOLLYS
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A girl is distressed about the troops, and someone concludes this is a fair deduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the girl's name round (SYLLOM) in this down clue; 'about' wraps it round the American soldiers. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllogism is a form of deductive argument drawing a conclusion from two premises.

clue.text: Stretcher cases may be put on it

definitions.meaning: a torture device that stretches its victim's body

definitions.text: cases may be put on it
definitions.meaning: a frame or shelf on which luggage or bottles are stored

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' suggests a hospital stretcher carrying cases (patients); it is the torture instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval torture frame stretched the body, and a luggage shelf or frame holds suitcases.

clue.text: Damage trains do under part of arch

indicators.note: damage here is an instruction to wreck the following letters and rebuild them in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone vandalises the trains, damaging the underside of a railway arch.
explanation.definitionFit: The intrados is the inner curve or underside of an arch, as opposed to the outer extrados.

clue.text: Poet's all-round achievement in American sport

definitions.meaning: the ancient Greek epic poet of the Iliad and Odyssey
in baseball, a hit letting the batter run round all the bases

explanation.walkthrough: 'all-round' means going round every base, not versatile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek bard shares his name with baseball slang for a home run, a circuit of all four bases.

clue.text: No aims in organisation — hence this restlessness?

indicators.note: organisation here means arranging the letters of the preceding words into a new order

explanation.surface: Lying awake with no goals, one wonders whether purposelessness is what causes the sleepless nights.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' belongs to the letters being rearranged, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is habitual sleeplessness, a restless inability to settle at night.

clue.text: In sacred works, it's a problem for organ

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a body of sacred writings
it's expands to it is

explanation.surface: A complaint in the scriptures about a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks like the church instrument but means a body organ, the ear; 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Otitis is inflammation of the ear, an ailment of that hearing organ.

clue.text: Evil edict appearing funny to wit

indicators.note: funny here means odd or peculiar, telling us the letters of the two preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A wicked decree that turns out to be comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Videlicet is Latin for namely, abbreviated viz, used to introduce an example or specification.

clue.text: Artist not quite ready with the last of the rent

indicators.note: not quite means the word for ready is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: ready (often readies) is slang for cash

indicators.note: the last of points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A struggling painter is short of cash when the rent falls due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for money; 'not quite' trims it to MONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of the Water Lilies series.

clue.text: Naval commander in the hold

definitions.meaning: the British admiral who died at Trafalgar
a wrestling grip applied from behind under the arms

explanation.walkthrough: 'in the hold' paints a ship's cargo hold; 'hold' is the wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Horatio of Trafalgar fame, and a wrestling grip (full or half) are both called this.

clue.text: Remove for burial, using implement

definitions.meaning: to bear a body out, as a coffin is taken away to be buried
implement as a verb, to execute or put into effect

explanation.walkthrough: 'implement' reads as a noun (a tool) but is the verb meaning to execute.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something away, as a coffin, and to execute or accomplish a plan share the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Tea, say, provided with a bit of fish?

definitions.text: Tea, say, provided with a bit of fish?

indicators.note: say tells us to take the word tea as spoken, giving the name of the letter it sounds like

parts.note: tea is pronounced like the letter T
provided means if, as in on condition that
a fin is one part of a fish

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea is served with a little fish on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a tiffin is a light meal, and tea with some fish fits.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglo-Indian usage a tiffin is a light midday meal or snack, so a tea with fish qualifies.

clue.text: Firmly securing a thing

definitions.meaning: the act of fastening or attaching something firmly
as in having a thing about something, an obsession

explanation.walkthrough: 'a thing' is the idiom for an obsession, as in having a thing about someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastening something in place, and an obsessive preoccupation, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Bustopher's male relative? A novel hero

definitions.meaning: Bustopher Jones is a cat in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum poems; a male cat is a tom, so a tom of the Jones family
the foundling hero of Henry Fielding's 1749 comic novel

explanation.walkthrough: Bustopher Jones is the fat clubland cat in T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A male cat surnamed like Eliot's Bustopher, and Fielding's eponymous foundling, share this name.

clue.text: Rich traveller's black dog

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A wealthy tourist owns a dark-coated hound.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are wealthy, fashionable people who fly from one resort to another.

clue.text: Plant a variety of hops in Deal, perhaps

indicators.note: a variety of suggests a different arrangement of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: A grower in the Kent town of Deal might cultivate several kinds of hops.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a Kent coastal town; Kent is England's hop-growing county. 'perhaps' just softens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-family flowering plant, in legend growing in the Elysian fields.

clue.text: Saw one's chance, finally, to make the most of something

parts.note: a saw is an old saying, a maxim
one is I, and one's expands to one is, giving IS

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word chance

explanation.surface: Someone spotted an opportunity at last and seized it to the full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense verb but is a noun meaning a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: To maximise something is to increase it to the greatest possible extent or exploit it fully.

clue.text: Sweet little creature hiding second animal, we hear

indicators.note: hiding means the small creature encloses the abbreviation for second

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A tiny rodent conceals a second beast, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animal, we hear' gives a second route: the answer sounds like MOOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mousse is a light, frothy dessert made with whipped cream or egg whites.

clue.text: Criticise a policy pronouncement

indicators.note: pronouncement tells us the phrase is to be heard when spoken

parts.note: a tack is a course of action or policy, so a policy is a tack

explanation.surface: A politician condemns a government statement on strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronouncement' looks like a statement of policy but signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack someone verbally is to criticise them harshly.

clue.text: It's crucial to get some money for tonic

parts.note: key means crucial or vital
a note is a piece of paper money

explanation.surface: Someone claims some cash is vital for a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tonic' looks like a reviving drink; in music it is the first note of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the keynote is the first degree of the scale, also called the tonic.

clue.text: Not fully stretched, we hear, without proper education

indicators.note: we hear marks the phrase as spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: not taut, a rope that is slack

explanation.surface: An underachieving pupil is described as never fully pushed and poorly schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fully stretched' sounds like a lazy student but means a rope that is not tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untaught has received no instruction or schooling.

clue.text: Muslim theologists among rule makers

indicators.note: among tells us the answer lies inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Islamic scholars count among those who make laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulema are the body of Muslim scholars trained in Islamic law and theology.

clue.text: State in which old character needs backing, in extremes of poverty

indicators.note: in places the reversed character between the outer letters of poverty
extremes of picks the first and last letters of the word poverty
needs backing tells us the word for the old character is written in reverse

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet

explanation.surface: A destitute nation whose ancient people must be supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs backing' reverses the ancient letter (ENUR); 'in' sets it between the outer letters of poverty. 'in which' after State is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Penury is a condition of extreme poverty and destitution.

clue.text: Not under control, yet in hand

definitions.meaning: not led or guided, lacking leadership
in card games, a card not yet played to a trick stays in the player's hand

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves seem to contradict; the second is about cards, where one not yet led is still in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking guidance, and of a playing card, still held because nobody has played it to the trick yet.

clue.text: Brothers and sisters are never so just

definitions.text: Brothers and sisters are never so
definitions.meaning: a sibling can never be a child without brothers or sisters
just in the sense of merely

explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like fair; it means merely.
explanation.definitionFit: A child with siblings can never be the single child of the family; merely or simply is a synonym too.

clue.text: School for point-to-points

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
taken as written
W and E, west and east, are two more compass points

explanation.surface: A school known for its horse races.
explanation.walkthrough: Point-to-points are amateur steeplechases; Stowe is an English public school in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowe is a well-known independent boarding school in Buckinghamshire, England.

clue.text: Gift with lines old sculptor displayed

parts.note: to gift is to give or donate
L is the abbreviation for line; LL for lines

explanation.surface: A present with an inscription, by an old sculptor, is put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gift' is a verb here, to give.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was the Florentine Renaissance sculptor of the bronze David.

clue.text: Way to overcome current obstacle in Wall Game

parts.note: a bailey is the outer wall of a castle
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A tactic for getting past an obstacle in the Eton Wall Game.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wall Game is played at Eton; here Wall and Game are separate pieces. The current is a river's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bailey bridge is a prefabricated military bridge for crossing rivers and other gaps.
